title: Astrophysics foundation model flags a galaxy implying a 210 Mpc ionized structure at z=6.8
summary: Using an astrophysics foundation model trained for JWST datasets, the authors identify a luminous galaxy at z=7.567 with Lyman-alpha transmission at z=6.80 +/- 0.07, indicating an ionized structure of 210.5 (+55.7/-53.5) comoving Mpc with a neutral fraction of about 2.07e-6. Simulations give a probability of about 1e-5 for a random sightline, and no significant galaxy overdensity is found. This is a version 1 preprint abstract of a single object, and the role of the model in selection should be confirmed from the Methods.
ai_technology: Astrophysics foundation model trained for JWST datasets used to identify the galaxy and its Lyman-alpha transmission

evidence.tested: JWST spectroscopic measurement compared with cosmological simulations; classified as retrospective or benchmark because it does not test a model prediction.
evidence.unknown: Confirmation of the claim by independent data, the exact role of the model in the selection, and the effect on reionization models; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Identifies the candidate object in JWST data from which the ionized structure is inferred.

source_review.scope: Version 1 abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI; author affiliations not retrieved. Full text not accessed. Author affiliations from OpenAlex metadata.
